titular: Big chipmakers and Microsoft to buy $26bn of Anthropic shares
resum: On top of its IPO, Anthropic will sell $26bn of shares at the offer price to AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC, according to CNBC. The maker of Claude is seeking up to $64bn in total and will list on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT.
per_que_importa: Having chip and cloud suppliers also be shareholders shows how intertwined the AI business is: if it goes well, everyone wins, but if it stalls, the blow is shared among many big companies.

titular: CoreWeave has its best day since 2025 and revives AI stocks
resum: The company that rents out computing power for AI rose 24.71% on Wednesday. It took in about $3.66bn in the third quarter (+168%), raised its full-year forecast to $13.0–13.3bn and has a $132.5bn backlog of contracts, although it is still losing money.
per_que_importa: CoreWeave is a barometer of AI spending: if its customers keep paying, data-centre investment is carrying on. But before these results the shares had fallen 40% in a month on worries about its debt.
xifra_text: CoreWeave's gain on Wednesday, its biggest since April 2025

titular: ChatGPT opens its doors to shops and sponsored ads
resum: OpenAI has launched a beta space where businesses can manage how they appear in ChatGPT: they can add their products and prices and see how often they are mentioned. In the US, online shops can also create their own assistant and pay to have it featured, in a format kept separate from normal answers.
per_que_importa: ChatGPT has about 1.2 billion weekly users: if it becomes a shop window, businesses will have to pay to be visible, as happens with Google. For users, it will matter to tell a recommendation apart from an ad.

titular: OpenAI buys AI travel agent Odessia and shuts it down
resum: OpenAI has bought Odessia, an assistant that booked trips using artificial intelligence, created by Sonder co-founder Francis Davidson, who is joining OpenAI. The service is closing, and travel company shares fell on the news.
per_que_importa: Big AI companies buy start-ups mainly to bring in their teams and technology. If ChatGPT ends up organising trips, travel agencies and booking platforms could lose customers and have to pay to stay visible.

titular: European Parliament wants to cut reliance on foreign cloud providers
resum: MEPs have presented a first report on the EU's Cloud and AI Development Act, which proposes common rules for data centres and artificial intelligence infrastructure. The aim is to depend less on big foreign providers, mainly American ones.
per_que_importa: Today almost all of Europe's digital services, from banks to hospitals, run on servers owned by US companies. A law like this could bring data-centre investment and jobs to Europe, but could also make some services pricier.

titular: From 2 December, AI-generated content in the EU must be labelled
resum: From 2 December, generative AI systems already on sale in the EU must mark the content they create so it can be detected as artificial. On the same date, the EU AI Act's bans on non-consensual intimate images and child abuse material take effect.
per_que_importa: Labelling AI content should help people tell a real photo or video from a fake, which is key against scams and disinformation. For tech companies, it means adapting their products and bearing the cost.

titular: Tesla overtakes Waymo in registered robotaxis in Texas, but not cars on the road
resum: According to Texas records, Tesla had 1,302 self-driving cars registered on 10 November, against 1,297 for Waymo, the Alphabet company. But being registered doesn't mean being on the road: in San Antonio, an independent tracker saw just one Tesla in service on launch day, while Waymo has about 100 there.
per_que_importa: Driverless taxis could make journeys cheaper, but they also threaten thousands of driving jobs. Each company's figures need careful reading: having cars registered is not the same as having them carry passengers.

titular: Kompanion, the start-up that wants to end small-business paperwork
resum: Young company Kompanion, which helps small businesses with administrative procedures, closed its first funding round of €800,000 in October. It has a team of nine and 150 customers in Spain.
per_que_importa: Red tape is one of the hidden costs that weigh most on the self-employed and small firms. Tools that automate it can free up hours for selling and producing, especially in businesses with no full-time administrator.
